newsitem.title: GERMANY: German city bans neo-Nazi march on Labour Day.
newsitem.headline: German city bans neo-Nazi march on Labour Day.

text.p: A large neo-Nazi rally planned for German Labour Day on May 1 in the eastern city of Leipzig has been banned, officials said on Wednesday.

They said they had prohibited the demonstration called by the right-wing National Democratic Party (NPD) because the German Trade Union Federation (DGB) had already scheduled a rally for the same day in the city centre.
"We simply do not have enough public space for the union and any other groups who want to demonstrate on May 1," said Helga Kaestner, director of the city's public order department.
She added that any counter-demonstrations protesting against the extreme right would also be banned. "Leipzig cannot tolerate that kind of disruption," Kaestner said.
But she warned that because the event had been publicised across the nation and on the Internet, the NPD was likely to submit a court appeal for permission to demonstrate, or to ignore the ban.
"The word has been spread throughout the country," she said. "We cannot consider the ban permanent yet because the NPD can still request a legal review of their case."
The NPD and its youth organisation drew about 5,000 demonstrators in February and March to protest in Munich against an exhibition documenting crimes of Hitler's Wehrmacht army.
